section.title: How to read this appendix
section.para: changes from the first edition This appendix collects, in one place, every rule of Lojban that this edition teaches differently from the first edition (1997, as corrected through its 1.1 revision – the corrections were errata, not rule changes). Each change is also marked where it is taught, with a status note; this appendix is the index of those notes. The governance story behind them is told in : in brief, a language-definition committee (the BPFK) and its parent organization (the LLG) adopted a small number of deliberate amendments between 2004 and 2016, and have been inactive since 2022, leaving the official language frozen as amended.
Every entry below carries one of these authority labels:

listitem.para: Ratified – adopted by an LLG vote. Only the article-system reform has this status.
Committee-approved – adopted by a recorded BPFK vote, never separately ratified by the LLG.
Checkpointed – fixed by the committee's 2004–2005 checkpoint process; the frozen snapshot texts of those dates are the authoritative statements.

De facto – never voted; the entry states its evidence class: a working document of the definition effort, implementation by the current tools surveyed for this edition, attested usage, or a combination. No one class by itself proves consensus.
Editorial – a convention this edition adopts where the official texts are silent or unsettled, always identified as such.

section.para: One promise made when the article reform was adopted extends in spirit to everything here: text written to the first edition's rules is not incorrect. It is older Lojban. This appendix exists so that readers can move between the two.

erratacorrections since the first edition Separately from the rule changes below, the successive revisions corrected genuine errors in the first edition's own Lojban – wrong words in printed examples, such as a le'u where a quotation opener lo'u was needed, a le ka for a le du'u , a mis-split na'e ke , and the like. Those were mistakes when printed and are simply fixed; they are not changes to the language and are not catalogued here.

One further change is to the book, not the language: the first edition printed the machine-oriented (YACC) grammar in full. This edition prints only the human-oriented EBNF grammar ( ); the machine grammars remain available as electronic supplements.

section.title: The article system (xorlo)
section.para:
xorlosummary of changes
Ratified (2004 checkpoint; adopted as the working baseline 2007; a fixed text ratified by LLG vote in 2020). The largest change in the book, taught in
and fundamental to . The first edition gave every description hidden default quantifiers ( lo broda meant su'o lo ro broda , le broda meant ro le su'o broda). All default quantifiers are abolished: an unquantified description is a constant, referring to whatever things the context supplies (formally, lo broda is zo'e noi ke'a broda). Consequences threaded through the book: lo is the everyday default article, referring to one or more things that really fit its description, with no implicit quantifier or count machinery; an outer quantifier, when actually said, selects distributively from a description's referents; an inner quantifier states the referents' count; PA broda means PA da poi broda and is no longer an abbreviation of PA lo broda ; the old mass doctrine (a mass has the properties of its components) is replaced by groups ( gunma) with collective satisfaction and their own properties; me is sharpened to is/are among the referents of ; and a number directly after la is part of the name, not an inner quantifier. The first edition's descriptor-attachment lessons that were derived from the abolished defaults are re-derived in
and .

listitem.para: dotsidechange summary Committee-approved (2015). Every cmevla is written with a leading and trailing dot, and the first edition's ban on la , lai , la'i , doi inside cmevla is lifted. Used throughout this edition.

consonant-glide-vowel banchange summary Committee-approved (27 December 2014; a transition-period vote predating the committee's 2015 reauthorization) and de facto (implemented in the surveyed word-form grammars). No word may contain a consonant directly followed by a glide: the first edition's kuarka and .niuport. are respelled ku'arka , .ni'uport.. See
and .

diphthongschange summary De facto (a working document of the definition effort, implemented in the surveyed parsers). Only ai, ei, oi, au are diphthongs; the first edition's other ten are glide-initial syllables, permitted word-initially or after a vowel. The same grammar makes word resolution deterministic (at each point the first matching rule wins, so a string of Lojban text breaks into words in exactly one way), extends the space of permitted experimental cmavo shapes, admits digits inside cmevla, and states per-class rules for consonantal syllables and stress. The full grammar is printed in this edition's appendices.

rafsiextended, change summary De facto (a working document of the definition effort, implemented in the surveyed parsers). Every fu'ivla has combining forms: unchanged in final position (a vowel-initial fu'ivla additionally takes a leading apostrophe when anything is attached before it), with 'y (or, when no collision arises, final-vowel-to- y substitution) elsewhere – always subject to the whole result still breaking apart into the intended words. The first edition confined fu'ivla to zei compounds and printed a never-adopted cultural-fu'ivla proposal in its place. See .

hyphenschange summary Editorial norm, de facto acceptance (implemented in the surveyed parsers). This edition keeps the classical minimal hyphen-placement rules for writing; the working grammar deliberately also accepts unneeded hyphens, and a 2019 attempt to make that official for the previous revision was vetoed.

commachange summary Editorial, following the working grammar. The comma is purely a pronunciation aid: it cannot license otherwise-invalid letter sequences, reversing several first-edition lessons that leaned on it. See .

tagsbinding change summary Committee-approved (2016). A tense or modal tag directly before a selbri binds to that selbri exactly as cu would – unless an explicit ku ends the tag construct first: lo nu broda ba brode is a complete bridi. The first edition's grammar absorbed such tags into the preceding construct. See
and the elision guidance in .

magic wordschange summary Checkpointed per word (2005), synthesis editorial. The quoting and binding words ( zo, zoi, la'o, lo'u, zei, bu) each received a fixed left-to-right conflict rule, replacing the first edition's inconsistent pairwise list; this edition presents them under one uniform principle and flags its two contested corners. The first edition's zo le'u loophole is gone. Erasure was never voted: si as taught is de facto (implemented alike in the surveyed parsers); su is de facto but unevenly implemented (the surveyed parsers disagree on whether it erases past a paragraph boundary); sa remains unsettled. See .

fi'orestriction changes summary De facto. Two of the first edition's parser restrictions on fi'o modals have lapsed (modal connectives and sticky modals now parse); direct negation still does not. See .

gekstags before, change summary De facto (implemented in the surveyed parsers; never voted). A tense or modal tag may now stand directly before a forethought connective ( pu ge broda gi brode ), read as a tag on the whole connected bridi; the first edition's grammar rejected this outright unless ke followed the tag. See .

section.title: Tenses
section.para: ZAhOchange summary Checkpointed (24 May 2004). An event contour used as a sumtcita is reversed from the first edition: in broda ba'o lo nu brode , it is the main bridi that carries the contour, located at the tagged event – the same as ba'o broda ca lo nu brode. First-edition text (including this book's own old examples) must be reread accordingly; contours used directly as tenses are unaffected, and the sentence-connective forms keep their first-edition meaning, so ZAhO is the one tense whose subordinate and coordinate forms use the same sentence order. See .

listitem.para: e-series attitudinalschange summary Editorial, following usage (from a committee rework never put to a vote): .e'e is exhortation (first edition: competence), .e'i is command (first edition: constraint); the .e'o scale's opposite is now offer, and .ai nai is unintentionality rather than refusal. The frozen official word lists keep the old senses; expect them in older text. See .

BAIchange summary Checkpointed (16 June 2005). The committee restated every BAI place by place, and no BAI's basic relation was reversed – but the restatement was not empty: it filled in meanings for some thirty converted BAI (forms like te pi'o ) that the first edition's tables left blank, revised the place order of tai , tightened several glosses to the checkpointed wording (notably ti'u , a time-of-day stamp), and settled the old reading dispute over BAI-plus- -nai in this book's favor. See .

letteralschange summary Checkpointed (2005). Shift words are bounded to their letteral string; .ybu is recognized as a unit before any word-level processing; the bu rules were fixed by exception list, with two corners where this edition follows the later synthesis instead. See .

terminologychanges of, in this edition Editorial. This edition says group where the first edition said mass; adopts the community term zi'evla for free-form borrowings; and uses cmevla for the name-word class throughout.

section.title: Debated but not changed
section.para: Readers who have followed community discussion may expect changes that this edition deliberately does not make, because nothing was ever adopted:

listitem.para: nascope of, unchanged na before the selbri still negates the whole bridi; the narrower in-place-scope proposal was never adopted (though the positions of na relative to a tense now do differ – a de facto resolution taught in ).

roexistential import, unchanged Restricted universal claims ( ro da poi broda) still carry existential import, presented in this edition as presuppositional; the vacuous-truth alternative was never settled. See .

distance tensesmedium readings, unchanged The middle members of the space/time distance and interval series ( va, za, ve'a, ze'a) keep their first-edition medium readings; a regularization to unspecified circulated as a proposal only. See .
termsetsunchanged Termsets remain official; a proposal to eliminate them was not adopted.
lo'eunsettled status le'eunsettled status jeiunsettled status lo'e , le'e , and jei remain as unsettled as the first edition left them, and are so marked where taught.
